newsitem.title: FINLAND: Forest rally helps Helsinki in run-up to results.
newsitem.headline: Forest rally helps Helsinki in run-up to results.

text.p: Shares rose on Tuesday on sharp gains in forestries, outperforming amid a steady flow of upbeat H1 reports. Brokers said the market was cautiously optimistic ahead of Merita, Enso H1 reports before Wednesday's open.

The FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark closed up 1.19 percent at 1,250, the HEX general index adding 0.86 percent to 3,632. Volume was slightly thinner than of late at 623 million markka, about one-third in Nokia with the action in forestries.
UPM Kymmene led gains, fuelled by recent broker upgrades and aided by a bright report from Sweden's AssiDoman. Attracting over 20 percent of trade, it rose 5.30 markka to 143.50.

UPM is due to report on Thursday. Enso, which comes before the open on Wednesday, put on 1.50 markka in thin dealings to 51.50. But Metsa-Serla, which came in last week at the top end of forecasts, picked up 1.80 markka to 51.20 in solid volume.
Enso's H1 profit is seen around 955 million markka.
"Forestries are hot, prices are rising and volumes growing, but I don't think gains will carry on long," one broker said. "For further gains the results would have to be really good."
Merita was little changed ahead of its H1 report, also due before Wednesday's open, ending down 0.20 markka at 22.70. The bank is expected to show a H1 bounce to about FIM 1.5 bln.

"Investors didn't do much as they got a bit edgy about tomorrow's results," another broker said, pointing to market disappointment in Stockholm as Swedish S-E Banken's H1 report came in below expectations.
